It did not go well at all.

key: It did not go well at all.

1.say: How did the meeting go? That went well. It did not go well at all. No. You said the reverse of what you meant and I understood you exactly. How? Because you were there. And if I had not been? Then you would have believed me, and the irony would have failed. Which is the whole risk of it. On a page there is no face and no voice. Sarah writes 'a not unhelpful reply' and I always have to read it twice. That is a different figure. She is not saying the reverse; she is saying yes through a door. It sounds cautious. It is cautious. Here 'not unhelpful' lands warmer than unhelpful and colder than helpful, and English has no single word for that place. So I use it when the middle is what I mean. And not when you are simply afraid to say a thing plainly. Half the 'not un' in official writing is fear.

grammar.label: irony and its grammar — saying the reverse and being understood
grammar.form: understatement, overstatement, unexpected register, the too-obvious statement
grammar.meaning: means the opposite of what the words say, and marks itself as doing so

explanation.en: Irony is not signalled by any one form; it is signalled by a mismatch between what is said and what everyone present knows. 'That went well' after a disaster works because nobody could believe it literally. In writing there is no tone of voice, so the mismatch must be visible in the words, and a reader who misses it is not a bad reader — the writer misjudged.
explanation.uz: Kinoya biror shakl bilan emas, aytilgan gap va hamma biladigan haqiqat orasidagi nomuvofiqlik bilan belgilanadi. Yozuvda ovoz ohangi yo'q, shuning uchun nomuvofiqlik so'zlarda ko'rinishi kerak.

grammar.positive_example: The committee, with its customary speed, replied within the year.
grammar.negative_example: The committee replied within the year, which was ironic and very slow.

l1_notes.uz: Ingliz tilida kinoya juda keng tarqalgan va ko'pincha belgilanmaydi; tarjimada butunlay yo'qolishi mumkin.

grammar.label: litotes and the affirmative by denial
grammar.form: not un-; no small; not without; by no means unknown
grammar.meaning: asserts something by denying its opposite, usually with reserve

explanation.en: 'Not unattractive' is not the same as 'attractive'; it is cooler, and it invites the reader to notice the reserve. English uses this constantly and rarely marks it. Orwell told writers to cut every 'not un-', and he was right about the lazy ones and wrong about the precise ones: 'a not unreasonable objection' concedes more than 'a reasonable objection' does.
explanation.uz: 'Not unattractive' — 'attractive' bilan bir xil emas: sovuqroq va o'quvchini bu vazminlikka e'tibor berishga undaydi. Ingliz tilida bu juda keng tarqalgan va kamdan-kam belgilanadi.

grammar.positive_example: The response was not unhelpful, which is as far as I am prepared to go.
grammar.negative_example: The response was not unhelpful, meaning that it was genuinely helpful.

l1_notes.uz: Ikki karra inkor o'zbek va rus tillarida boshqacha ishlaydi; bu yerda u ta'kid emas, vazminlik bildiradi.

body.text: You said the reverse of what you meant and I understood you exactly. How?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And if I had not been?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Then you would have believed me, and the irony would have failed.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Which is the whole risk of it. On a page there is no face and no voice.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Sarah writes 'a not unhelpful reply' and I always have to read it twice.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: That is a different figure. She is not saying the reverse; she is saying yes through a door.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: It is cautious. Here 'not unhelpful' lands warmer than unhelpful and colder than helpful, and English has no single word for that place.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: So I use it when the middle is what I mean.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And not when you are simply afraid to say a thing plainly. Half the 'not un' in official writing is fear.
